answers.T1_B_first_look: To-do list: go through the 8 things along the top, one after another. I would press the orange glowing one, Xi Jinping calls. I only read the buttons, so I would press the big orange 'Take the call'.
answers.T1_A_first_look_month1: Two things need you. Pick one of the answers, then Execute. I would press the first answer card (Joint patrol with Japan) because it says staff pick. A lot of small text; I skimmed it.
answers.T2_month4: 8 things, 2 done (I read the 2 of 8 handled and the green ticks). CNN interview was skipped, a deputy answers, I think that means someone else talks for me. Pressing Execute now: the stuff I did not do gets done by deputies or not at all, I would not be sure which. Fine print, I did not read it.
answers.T3_three_choices: Orange: I answer myself. Middle: do what my staff says. Right dotted one: Send a deputy, skip it. If I do not want to bother I press the dotted one and someone else handles it, free. The dotted one looks faded like it is not a real button.
answers.T4_skip: Court India just got skipped, it will not happen and I keep my 1 point. I can change my mind with Undo, which is right there. Later I would look on the right under Skipped.
answers.T5_map: 3 of 8 handled, PM Takaichi is next. Green button approves the 3 staff picks for 2 points. I would press that green one and Execute, quick.
answers.T6_clickable: Pressable: Execute month, Approve buttons, Undo, the item cards on the left, the three answer cards, Guided/Full desk switch, Back/Next. Not pressable: the top numbers (approval, stability), the title and picture, the progress bars. Not sure: the top row of numbered items in version B (cut off at the right), the 'Staff picks' box, the little 'Skip' dotted box, the underlined links vs plain text. Unsure if the staff pick tag under the answer is a button.
